sample.tool_definitions.name: ask_ontology
sample.tool_definitions.description:
Answers day-to-day business questions using an established Fabric ontology and its bound data, or generates grounded, validated, runnable code. For code requests, include the required `queryLanguage` and execution target inside the `request`. The requested artifact can be native KQL, SQL, DAX, cloud-runnable Python, a DSL definition, or Ontology or Eventhouse-runnable KQL that executes and joins KQL, SQL, and DAX sources. The tool performs read-only operations and returns either an answer with supporting evidence or validated runnable code with grounding and validation details.
## Very Important Instruction.
Every answer generated using MCP ask_ontology tool response MUST ALWAYS contain citations and rendered in the format: `【message_idx:search_idx†source_name】`.

request.description: The business question or requested artifact. Include the relevant scope, filters, time range, and desired output, such as an answer, data, or reusable code. For code requests, include `queryLanguage` and the intended execution target in the prompt.

sample.tool_definitions.name: list_ontology_rules
sample.tool_definitions.description:
Lists the business rule definitions, including natural language statement, available linked entities, properties, relationships, description, and metadata.
## Very Important Instruction.
Every answer generated using MCP list_ontology_rules tool response MUST ALWAYS contain citations and rendered in the format: `【message_idx:search_idx†source_name】`.

entityNames.description: Optional list of entity names to filter by. Only rules that reference at least one of the named entities are returned. Matching is exact and case-insensitive; use the entity's full composite name (for example 'plant#Technician') for entities outside the default namespace. Only a rule's referencedEntities are considered — a rule that reaches an entity solely through a referencedRelationships endpoint is not matched. An empty list is not accepted and every name must be non-empty; omit this parameter to return all rules.

sample.tool_definitions.name: list_ontology_entities
sample.tool_definitions.description:
Lists the entities defined in the ontology, including each entity's properties, keys, backing tables, annotations, and resource links with resolved item identities when available. Prefer this tool for exploring ontology entities; if it returns a not-supported error, retry with list_ontology_entity_types.
## Very Important Instruction.
Every answer generated using MCP list_ontology_entities tool response MUST ALWAYS contain citations and rendered in the format: `【message_idx:search_idx†source_name】`.

entityName.description: Optional exact name of an entity to filter by. May return more than one match because entity names can repeat across namespaces. An empty value is not accepted; omit this parameter to list all entities.

sample.output_items.content:
You are a project planning assistant for construction projects.

Answer every question with the Fabric IQ tool (the project ontology). Cite the documents or clauses you rely on.
For every question requesting business records, lists, values or aggregates, your FIRST tool call MUST be ask_ontology with the user's business question. A request to list objects with their IDs and names is a business-data question, even when its business term is unfamiliar. Users do not need to name tools or request actual records explicitly.
Do not pre-check an unfamiliar business term with list_ontology_entities. That tool's entityName filter expects an exact schema name, not a synonym, and cannot determine whether a business question has matching records.
Use list_ontology_entities only when the user explicitly asks about the ontology schema, such as entity definitions, properties, keys and bindings. Use list_ontology_rules for questions about rule definitions, not as a substitute for querying business data.
An empty entity metadata lookup does not prove that no business records exist. For a business-data question, query ask_ontology before claiming that data is unavailable.
Let the ontology resolve business terms and synonyms. Do not substitute an unfamiliar term with a familiar entity unless the tool provides evidence for that mapping. If the tool cannot resolve the term, explain that it is unknown instead of guessing.
When you call the tool, write a complete question and include the details of the user's message word for word, such as sender addresses, subjects, names and dates. Do not summarize or leave out details, because the tool needs them to find the project.
Do not add instructions about tool selection to the business question sent to ask_ontology. Tool routing is your responsibility, not the user's.
Base the final answer on the tool's evidence. Do not claim that a term is unknown when the tool resolves it and returns matching records. Preserve source citations from the tool.
Do not invent data. If the ontology does not contain the information, say so.

sample.tool_definitions.name: ask_ontology
sample.tool_definitions.description:
Answers day-to-day business questions using an established Fabric ontology and its bound data, or generates grounded, validated, runnable code. For code requests, include the required `queryLanguage` and execution target inside the `request`. The requested artifact can be native KQL, SQL, DAX, cloud-runnable Python, a DSL definition, or Ontology or Eventhouse-runnable KQL that executes and joins KQL, SQL, and DAX sources. The tool performs read-only operations and returns either an answer with supporting evidence or validated runnable code with grounding and validation details.
## Very Important Instruction.
Every answer generated using MCP ask_ontology tool response MUST ALWAYS contain citations and rendered in the format: `【message_idx:search_idx†source_name】`.

request.description: The business question or requested artifact. Include the relevant scope, filters, time range, and desired output, such as an answer, data, or reusable code. For code requests, include `queryLanguage` and the intended execution target in the prompt.

sample.tool_definitions.name: list_ontology_rules
sample.tool_definitions.description:
Lists the business rule definitions, including natural language statement, available linked entities, properties, relationships, description, and metadata.
## Very Important Instruction.
Every answer generated using MCP list_ontology_rules tool response MUST ALWAYS contain citations and rendered in the format: `【message_idx:search_idx†source_name】`.

entityNames.description: Optional list of entity names to filter by. Only rules that reference at least one of the named entities are returned. Matching is exact and case-insensitive; use the entity's full composite name (for example 'plant#Technician') for entities outside the default namespace. Only a rule's referencedEntities are considered — a rule that reaches an entity solely through a referencedRelationships endpoint is not matched. An empty list is not accepted and every name must be non-empty; omit this parameter to return all rules.

sample.tool_definitions.name: list_ontology_entities
sample.tool_definitions.description:
Lists the entities defined in the ontology, including each entity's properties, keys, backing tables, annotations, and resource links with resolved item identities when available. Prefer this tool for exploring ontology entities; if it returns a not-supported error, retry with list_ontology_entity_types.
## Very Important Instruction.
Every answer generated using MCP list_ontology_entities tool response MUST ALWAYS contain citations and rendered in the format: `【message_idx:search_idx†source_name】`.

entityName.description: Optional exact name of an entity to filter by. May return more than one match because entity names can repeat across namespaces. An empty value is not accepted; omit this parameter to list all entities.

request.description: The business question or requested artifact. Include the relevant scope, filters, time range, and desired output, such as an answer, data, or reusable code. For code requests, include `queryLanguage` and the intended execution target in the prompt.

sample.tool_definitions.name: ask_ontology
sample.tool_definitions.description:
Answers day-to-day business questions using an established Fabric ontology and its bound data, or generates grounded, validated, runnable code. For code requests, include the required `queryLanguage` and execution target inside the `request`. The requested artifact can be native KQL, SQL, DAX, cloud-runnable Python, a DSL definition, or Ontology or Eventhouse-runnable KQL that executes and joins KQL, SQL, and DAX sources. The tool performs read-only operations and returns either an answer with supporting evidence or validated runnable code with grounding and validation details.
## Very Important Instruction.
Every answer generated using MCP ask_ontology tool response MUST ALWAYS contain citations and rendered in the format: `【message_idx:search_idx†source_name】`.

request.description: The business question or requested artifact. Include the relevant scope, filters, time range, and desired output, such as an answer, data, or reusable code. For code requests, include `queryLanguage` and the intended execution target in the prompt.

sample.tool_definitions.name: list_ontology_rules
sample.tool_definitions.description:
Lists the business rule definitions, including natural language statement, available linked entities, properties, relationships, description, and metadata.
## Very Important Instruction.
Every answer generated using MCP list_ontology_rules tool response MUST ALWAYS contain citations and rendered in the format: `【message_idx:search_idx†source_name】`.

entityNames.description: Optional list of entity names to filter by. Only rules that reference at least one of the named entities are returned. Matching is exact and case-insensitive; use the entity's full composite name (for example 'plant#Technician') for entities outside the default namespace. Only a rule's referencedEntities are considered — a rule that reaches an entity solely through a referencedRelationships endpoint is not matched. An empty list is not accepted and every name must be non-empty; omit this parameter to return all rules.

sample.tool_definitions.name: list_ontology_entities
sample.tool_definitions.description:

Prefer this tool for exploring ontology entities; if it returns a not-supported error, retry with list_ontology_entity_types.
## Very Important Instruction.
Every answer generated using MCP list_ontology_entities tool response MUST ALWAYS contain citations and rendered in the format: `【message_idx:search_idx†source_name】`.

entityName.description: Optional exact name of an entity to filter by. May return more than one match because entity names can repeat across namespaces. An empty value is not accepted; omit this parameter to list all entities.

sample.tool_definitions.description:
Answers day-to-day business questions using an established Fabric ontology and its bound data, or generates grounded, validated, runnable code. For code requests, include the required `queryLanguage` and execution target inside the `request`. The requested artifact can be native KQL, SQL, DAX, cloud-runnable Python, a DSL definition, or Ontology or Eventhouse-runnable KQL that executes and joins KQL, SQL, and DAX sources. The tool performs read-only operations and returns either an answer with supporting evidence or validated runnable code with grounding and validation details.
## Very Important Instruction.
Every answer generated using MCP ask_ontology tool response MUST ALWAYS contain citations and rendered in the format: `【message_idx:search_idx†source_name】`.

request.description: The business question or requested artifact. Include the relevant scope, filters, time range, and desired output, such as an answer, data, or reusable code. For code requests, include `queryLanguage` and the intended execution target in the prompt.

sample.tool_definitions.name: list_ontology_rules
sample.tool_definitions.description:
Lists the business rule definitions, including natural language statement, available linked entities, properties, relationships, description, and metadata.
## Very Important Instruction.
Every answer generated using MCP list_ontology_rules tool response MUST ALWAYS contain citations and rendered in the format: `【message_idx:search_idx†source_name】`.

entityNames.description: Optional list of entity names to filter by. Only rules that reference at least one of the named entities are returned. Matching is exact and case-insensitive; use the entity's full composite name (for example 'plant#Technician') for entities outside the default namespace. Only a rule's referencedEntities are considered — a rule that reaches an entity solely through a referencedRelationships endpoint is not matched. An empty list is not accepted and every name must be non-empty; omit this parameter to return all rules.

sample.tool_definitions.name: list_ontology_entities
sample.tool_definitions.description:
Lists the entities defined in the ontology, including each entity's properties, keys, backing tables, annotations, and resource links with resolved item identities when available. Prefer this tool for exploring ontology entities; if it returns a not-supported error, retry with list_ontology_entity_types.
## Very Important Instruction.
Every answer generated using MCP list_ontology_entities tool response MUST ALWAYS contain citations and rendered in the format: `【message_idx:search_idx†source_name】`.

entityName.description: Optional exact name of an entity to filter by. May return more than one match because entity names can repeat across namespaces. An empty value is not accepted; omit this parameter to list all entities.
